title: Tomb Raider
knownFacts: Lara Croft was designed by Toby Gard.
The character was originally named Lara Cruz before being changed to Lara Croft.
The game sold over 7 million copies worldwide.
Developed in approximately 18 months.
The Scion artifact is fragmented across Peru, Greece, Egypt, and Atlantis.
The game's success directly spawned the multimedia Tomb Raider franchise.

title: Tomb Raider II
knownFacts: The first Tomb Raider game to feature vehicles, including a speedboat and snowmobile.
Venice sequences required designing first underwater urban environments for the series.
Sold over 8 million copies, outselling the original at launch.
The Great Wall of China opens the game, establishing a faster-paced tone.
Marco Bartoli is the main antagonist.
The game introduced Lara's home base sequences at Croft Manor.

title: Tomb Raider III
knownFacts: Features non-linear level order — players can choose between India, South Pacific, London, and Nevada before Antarctica.
Known for its high difficulty, including levels in the London sewers and Area 51.
Dr. Willard is the primary antagonist.
The meteor artifact fragments are tied to mutation and ancient power.
One of the longest games in the classic trilogy by level count.
Contains hidden shortcuts and alternate paths not found in previous entries.

title: Tomb Raider: The Last Revelation
knownFacts: Almost entirely set in Egypt, exploring Luxor, Karnak, Alexandria, and the Giza Plateau.
Introduced a young Lara prologue set in Cambodia.
Werner Von Croy appears as both mentor and antagonist.
Uses a hub-and-spoke structure connecting several Egyptian sites.
The ending implied Lara's death, controversially.
Engine received upgrades including improved lighting and trap sequences.

title: Tomb Raider Chronicles
engine: Proprietary (Core Design, The Last Revelation engine)
knownFacts: Structured as four flashback episodes recounted by Lara's friends at her memorial.
Features a teenage Lara in a supernatural episode set on an island.
Rome, a Russian submarine, Black Isle, and a skyscraper in Hamburg are the settings.
Reused engine and assets from The Last Revelation.
Bridged the classic era before a planned next-generation reinvention.
Regarded as a transitional entry rather than a full sequel.

title: Tomb Raider: The Angel of Darkness
knownFacts: Kurtis Trent is a secondary playable character with telekinetic abilities.
Originally planned as the first of a trilogy; sequel plans were cancelled after poor reception.
Suffered a troubled development cycle with repeated scope changes.
The Obscura Paintings and the Cabal are the central mystery.
Received poorly at launch for bugs and control issues but has since gained a cult following.
Marks the end of Core Design's involvement with the main Tomb Raider series.

title: Tomb Raider: Legend
knownFacts: First Tomb Raider game developed by Crystal Dynamics, who had previously made Legacy of Kain.
Introduced the grapple as a traversal tool.
Received strong critical acclaim, revitalizing the series after Angel of Darkness.
The game connects Arthurian mythology with the mystery of Lara's mother.
Radio-support characters Zip and Alister provide real-time commentary during expeditions.
Sold over 2.5 million copies in its first month.

title: Tomb Raider: Anniversary
knownFacts: Released to mark the 10th anniversary of the original 1996 game.
Originally a collaboration with Buzz Monkey Software before Crystal Dynamics took full control.
Deepened Lara's conflict with Jacqueline Natla and expanded her motivation.
The adrenaline dodge mechanic was introduced for boss encounters.
Levels reinterpret rather than recreate original rooms with Legend-era movement.
Bridges the Legend and Underworld entries in the Crystal Dynamics trilogy.

title: Tomb Raider: Underworld
knownFacts: Concludes the Legend trilogy, resolving storylines from both Legend and Anniversary.
Thailand was widely praised as a visual high point of the series.
Features a Lara doppelganger created by Natla.
Downloadable content episodes Beneath the Ashes and Lara's Shadow extended the story on Xbox 360.
Sold approximately 2.6 million units but was considered a commercial underperformance.
Introduced more physics-based puzzle interactions and climbing mechanics.

title: Tomb Raider
knownFacts: Origin story reboot; begins the Survivor trilogy.
Yamatai is a fictional island based loosely on historical Japan.
Over 11 million copies sold by 2016.
Used performance capture for Camilla Luddington as Lara.
Optional tombs were introduced as compact side-puzzle areas.
Multiplayer mode was included but later considered a low point of the release.

title: Rise of the Tomb Raider
knownFacts: Timed exclusive on Xbox One before releasing on PlayStation 4.
Kitezh draws from the Russian legend of a submerged holy city.
Significantly expanded the optional challenge tomb system.
Over 7 million copies sold by 2018.
Blood Ties DLC added first-person exploration of Croft Manor.
Features Trinity as the primary antagonistic organization throughout the Survivor trilogy.

title: Shadow of the Tomb Raider
knownFacts: First main Tomb Raider game developed by Eidos-Montréal rather than Crystal Dynamics.
Paititi is the largest hub area in the Survivor trilogy.
Draws from Mayan and Aztec mythology for its apocalypse narrative.
Introduced expanded difficulty sliders for combat, exploration, and puzzles independently.
Underwater traversal received the most emphasis of any entry in the trilogy.
Concludes the Survivor trilogy arc and Lara's conflict with Trinity.
